items.q: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: El과 Jo는 반에서 가장 키가 큰 학생들이었다.
El과 Jo는 화분에 쉽게 손이 닿았다.
El은 혼자서 식물에 물을 줄 수 있었다.
El과 Jo는 반에서 가장 키가 작은 학생들이었다.
items.exp: El과 Jo는 반에서 가장 작은 학생들이어서 화분에 혼자서는 손이 닿지 않아 늘 함께 물을 주었어요.
items.passage: El and Jo were the smallest students in the class. They were always together. They even watered the plants together in the class because they could not reach the pots alone.

items.q: 밑줄 친 빈도부사의 위치가 어색한 것은?
items.exp: 빈도부사는 일반동사 앞, 조동사와 be동사 뒤에 와요. 따라서 They usually play soccer on Sundays.가 되어야 해요.
items.passage: They were [always] together.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?

They watered the plants together ___ they could not reach the pots alone.
items.exp: 뒤에 「주어+동사」(they could not reach ~)가 오므로 접속사 because가 알맞아요. because of는 뒤에 명사(구)가 와요.
items.passage: El and Jo were the smallest students in the class. They were always together. They even watered the plants together in the class because they could not reach the pots alone.

items.q:
다음 질문에 대한 답으로 알맞은 것은?

Why did El and Jo water the plants together?
choices: Because the plants were very big.
Because they wanted to play outside.
Because they could not reach the pots alone.
items.exp: 두 사람은 혼자서는 화분에 손이 닿지 않아서(because they could not reach the pots alone) 함께 물을 주었어요.
items.passage: El and Jo were the smallest students in the class. They were always together. They even watered the plants together in the class because they could not reach the pots alone.

items.q:
(A), (B)에 들어갈 전치사가 바르게 짝지어진 것은?

(A) the spring, something was DIFFERENT.
(B) the last day of school, Mr. Diaz said ~.
items.exp: 계절 앞에는 전치사 in, 특정한 날 앞에는 전치사 on을 써요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 grew와 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: She grew tomatoes in the garden.
He grows rice on his farm.
items.exp: 본문의 grew TALLER는 「grow+형용사」로 '~해지다'라는 뜻이에요. It grew cold는 '추워졌다'로 같은 쓰임이고, 나머지는 '재배하다'라는 뜻이에요.
items.passage: Jo [grew] TALLER!

items.q: Jo was taller than El, so Jo could water the plants alone. 이 문장에서 Jo가 혼자 물을 줄 수 있었던 이유는?
choices: Jo가 El보다 나이가 더 많았기 때문이다.
El이 아파서 학교에 오지 않았기 때문이다.
Jo가 El보다 키가 더 컸기 때문이다.
items.exp: 접속사 so(그래서) 앞의 내용이 원인이에요. Jo가 El보다 키가 커서 혼자 물을 줄 수 있었어요.
items.passage: However, in the spring, something was DIFFERENT. Jo grew TALLER! Jo was taller than El, so Jo could water the plants alone. El felt smaller every day.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: My bag is heavier than yours.
This book is more interesting than that one.
Mina is younger than her sister.
Today is more hot than yesterday.
items.exp: hot은 짧은 단어라 hotter로 비교급을 만들어요. more hot은 틀려요.
items.passage: Jo was [taller than] El.

items.q: 밑줄 친 부분의 의미로 알맞은 것은?
choices: 날마다 점점 더 주눅이 드는 기분이 들었다.
items.exp: feel small은 '주눅이 들다, 초라한 기분이 들다'라는 뜻이에요. Jo는 키가 컸지만 El은 그렇지 못해서 점점 주눅이 들었어요.
items.passage: El [felt smaller every day].

items.q: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Diaz 선생님은 학생들에게 꽃을 학교에 두라고 했다.
Diaz 선생님은 첫날 꽃을 나누어 주었다.
학생들은 가을 동안 꽃을 돌보기로 했다.
Diaz 선생님은 학기 마지막 날 학생들에게 꽃을 집에 가져가 돌보라고 했다.
items.exp: Diaz 선생님은 학교의 마지막 날에 학생들이 꽃을 집에 가져가 여름 동안 돌봐도 된다고 했어요.
items.passage: On the last day of school, Mr. Diaz said, "Class, you can take a flower home and care for it over the summer." All the students ran to the window. El's classmates reached for the pots over tiny El. They took all the pots with colorful flowers. El took the last pot. It had the smallest plant with no flowers. "I feel just like you, little plant," said El.

items.q: 밑줄 친 can과 의미가 같은 것은?
items.exp: 본문의 can은 '~해도 된다'라는 허락의 의미예요. You can use my pen.의 can도 허락의 의미이고, 나머지는 '~할 수 있다'는 능력의 의미예요.
items.passage: Mr. Diaz said, "Class, you [can] take a flower home and care for it over the summer."

items.q: 밑줄 친 care for와 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것은?
items.exp: care for는 '~을 돌보다'라는 뜻이라 take care of, look after와 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
items.passage: you can take a flower home and [care for] it over the summer.

items.q: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: El의 반 친구들은 작은 El 위로 손을 뻗어 화분을 가져갔다.
El의 반 친구들은 El에게 화분을 양보했다.
학생들은 천천히 줄을 서서 화분을 가져갔다.
El의 반 친구들은 꽃이 없는 화분을 골랐다.
items.exp: 반 친구들은 작은 El 위로 손을 뻗어 꽃이 핀 화분을 모두 가져갔고, El은 마지막 화분을 가져갔어요.
items.passage: On the last day of school, Mr. Diaz said, "Class, you can take a flower home and care for it over the summer." All the students ran to the window. El's classmates reached for the pots over tiny El. They took all the pots with colorful flowers. El took the last pot. It had the smallest plant with no flowers. "I feel just like you, little plant," said El.

items.q: 밑줄 친 tiny와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
items.exp: tiny는 '아주 작은'이라는 뜻으로 very small과 가장 가까워요.
items.passage: El's classmates reached for the pots over [tiny] El.

items.q: 밑줄 친 with와 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: I went there with my friends.
Cut the paper with a knife.
She is the girl with long hair.
items.exp: 본문의 with는 '~을 가진'이라는 뜻이에요. the girl with long hair의 with도 '~을 가진'이라는 뜻이고, 나머지는 '~와 함께', '~으로(도구)'의 뜻이에요.
items.passage: They took all the pots [with] colorful flowers.

items.q: 밑줄 친 부분과 의미가 같은 것은?
choices: It had the smallest plant with many flowers.
It had the smallest plant with some flowers.
It had the smallest plant without any flowers.
It had the smallest plant without no flowers.
It had the smallest plant with a few flowers.
items.exp: with no+명사는 '~이 없는'이라는 뜻으로 without (any)+명사와 같아요.
items.passage: It had the smallest plant [with no flowers].

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?

El and Jo were the ___ students in the class.
items.exp: 「the+최상급+in+비교 범위」로 '반에서 가장 작은'은 the smallest예요.
items.passage: El and Jo were the [___] students in the class.

items.q: El이 밑줄 친 말을 한 이유로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 자신처럼 작고 꽃이 없는 식물에게 공감해서
items.exp: feel just like ~는 '~와 같은 기분이다'라는 뜻이에요. 작고 꽃이 없는 식물이 자신의 처지와 닮았다고 느꼈어요.
items.passage: El took the last pot. It had the smallest plant with no flowers. "I [feel just like you], little plant," said El.

items.q: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Diaz 선생님은 그 식물이 곧 시들 것이라고 말했다.
Diaz 선생님은 시간이 지나면 그 식물이 자라서 아름다운 꽃이 필 것이라고 말했다.
Diaz 선생님은 그 식물이 장미라고 말했다.
Diaz 선생님은 그 식물에 꽃이 이미 피었다고 말했다.
Diaz 선생님은 El에게 다른 화분을 가져가라고 했다.
items.exp: Diaz 선생님은 aster 식물이라고 알려 주며 In time, it'll grow and have beautiful flowers.라고 했어요.
items.passage: Mr. Diaz looked at El and said, "That's an aster plant. In time, it'll grow and have beautiful flowers." "But it's just a little green plant," said El. She was not so sure.

items.q: 밑줄 친 In time의 의미로 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: In time은 '시간이 지나면, 결국'이라는 뜻이에요. 'on time(제시간에)'과 헷갈리지 않도록 주의해요.
items.passage: "That's an aster plant. [In time], it'll grow and have beautiful flowers."

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?

In time, it'll grow and ___ beautiful flowers.
items.exp: and로 연결된 병렬 구조에서 will 뒤의 grow와 같은 형태인 동사원형 have를 써야 해요.
items.passage: In time, it'll grow and [___] beautiful flowers.

items.q: 밑줄 친 just와 같은 의미로 쓰인 것은?
items.exp: 본문의 just는 '단지, 그저'라는 뜻이에요. just one pen의 just도 '단지'라는 뜻이고, 나머지는 '방금'이라는 뜻이에요.
items.passage: "But it's [just] a little green plant," said El.

items.q: 밑줄 친 so의 의미로 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: not so sure에서 so는 정도를 나타내는 부사로 '그렇게'라는 뜻이에요. '그렇게 확신하지 못했다'라는 의미예요.
items.passage: She was not [so] sure.

items.q:
(A), (B), (C)의 so의 의미가 순서대로 바르게 짝지어진 것은?

(A) Jo was taller than El, so Jo could water the plants alone.
(B) She was not so sure.
(C) I'm so happy to see you.
items.exp: (A)는 접속사 '그래서', (B)는 정도의 부사 '그렇게', (C)는 강조의 부사 '너무'예요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 grandma's 뒤에 생략된 말로 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: 소유격 grandma's 뒤에 house가 생략되어 '할머니 댁'이라는 뜻이에요.
items.passage: "I'll be at my [grandma's] all summer."

items.q: Jo가 El에게 zinnia 식물을 주려는 이유로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Jo가 여름 내내 할머니 댁에 있을 것이라 직접 돌볼 수 없어서
items.exp: Jo는 I'll be at my grandma's all summer.라고 말했어요. 여름 내내 집을 비우므로 El에게 식물을 맡긴 거예요.
items.passage: "You can have my zinnia plant," Jo said to El, "I'll be at my grandma's all summer." "I'll plant my aster and your zinnia side by side," El said. "They'll be good friends ― just like us!" said Jo. El smiled.

items.q: 밑줄 친 side by side의 의미로 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: side by side는 '나란히'라는 뜻이에요.
items.passage: "I'll plant my aster and your zinnia [side by side]," El said.

items.q: 밑줄 친 They가 가리키는 것은?
items.exp: They는 바로 앞에서 El이 말한 my aster and your zinnia를 가리켜요.
items.passage: "[They]'ll be good friends ― just like us!" said Jo.

items.q: Jo가 밑줄 친 말을 한 의도로 알맞은 것은?
choices: 두 식물이 서로 싸울 것이라는 뜻이다.
El과 Jo가 서로 닮지 않았다는 뜻이다.
aster와 zinnia가 El과 Jo처럼 좋은 친구가 될 것이라는 뜻이다.
items.exp: just like us는 '꼭 우리처럼'이라는 뜻이에요. 두 식물이 El과 Jo처럼 좋은 친구가 될 거라는 의미예요.
items.passage: "They'll be good friends ― [just like us]!" said Jo.

items.q: 밑줄 친 It과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
choices: I bought a book. It is very interesting.
Where is my bag? It is under the desk.
This is my dog. It is so cute.
I lost my phone. It was new.
items.exp: 본문의 It은 시기를 나타내는 비인칭 주어로 '그것'으로 해석하지 않아요. It is Monday today.의 It도 요일을 나타내는 비인칭 주어이고, 나머지는 앞에 나온 대상을 가리키는 대명사예요.
items.passage: [It] was growing season.

items.q: 밑줄 친 It의 해석이 '그것'이 아닌 것은?
choices: I have a cat. [It] is white.
Where's my bag? [It] is on the sofa.
I like this song. [It] is great.
This is my pen. [It] was a gift.
items.exp: 시간을 나타내는 비인칭 주어 It은 '그것'으로 해석하지 않아요. 나머지 It은 앞에 나온 대상을 가리켜요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 them이 가리키는 것은?
items.exp: them은 El이 정원에 심은 the flowers(aster와 zinnia)를 가리켜요.
items.passage: El planted the flowers in her garden. All summer long, she cared for [them].

items.q: 다음 중 전치사의 쓰임이 틀린 문장은?
choices: It rains a lot in the spring.
I visited her on the last day of summer.
We had a party on my birthday.
items.exp: 요일이나 특정한 날 앞에는 전치사 on을 써서 on Monday가 되어야 해요.
items.passage: On the last day of summer, Jo came to El's house.

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: She opened the door and walked in.
We ran to the park and played soccer.
They sat down and ate lunch.
He went to the store and buys milk.
I got up and washed my face.
items.exp: and로 연결되는 동사는 같은 시제로 맞춰야 해요. went와 병렬이므로 buys가 아니라 bought가 되어야 해요.
items.passage: El and Jo ran to the garden and suddenly stopped.

items.q: 위 글의 마지막 부분에 대한 설명으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: aster에 꽃이 피어 있었고, El도 키가 자라 있었다.
items.exp: 여름의 마지막 날 정원에 가 보니 aster에 꽃이 피어 있었고, El도 키가 자랐어요(and El grew TALLER, TOO!).
items.passage: El planted the flowers in her garden. It was growing season. All summer long, she cared for them. On the last day of summer, Jo came to El's house. El and Jo ran to the garden and suddenly stopped. Something was DIFFERENT! There were flowers on the aster ... and El grew TALLER, TOO!

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은? (과거의 의미)

There ___ flowers on the aster.
items.exp: There were+복수 명사는 '~들이 있었다'라는 뜻이에요. flowers가 복수이고 과거이므로 were가 알맞아요.
items.passage: [There were] flowers on the aster ... and El grew TALLER, TOO!

items.q: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: There is a cat on the sofa.
There are three books on the desk.
There was a party last night.
There were many students in the park yesterday.
There is two apples in the basket.
items.exp: There is/are 뒤의 명사가 복수(two apples)이면 are를 써야 해요. There are two apples ~가 되어야 해요.
items.passage: There were flowers on the aster.

items.q: 밑줄 친 too와 같은 의미로 쓰인 것은?
choices: It is too heavy to carry.
This bag is too small for me.
I like pizza, and my brother likes it, too.
items.exp: 본문의 too는 문장 끝에 쓰여 '또한, ~도'라는 뜻이에요. 나머지는 '너무'라는 뜻이에요.
items.passage: ...and El grew TALLER, [TOO]!

items.q:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

Jo grew taller and could water the plants alone.
(A) El took the last pot with the smallest plant.
(B) On the last day of school, the students took flowers home.
(C) El felt smaller every day.
items.exp: Jo가 자라자 El은 점점 주눅이 들었고(C), 학교 마지막 날 학생들이 꽃을 가져갔으며(B), El은 마지막 화분을 가져갔어요(A).

items.q: 위 글의 주제로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 친구와 함께 식물을 가꾸며 함께 자라는 이야기
items.exp: El과 Jo는 서로 돕고 식물을 함께 가꾸며 키와 마음이 자라는 이야기예요.
items.passage: El and Jo were the smallest students in the class. They were always together. They even watered the plants together in the class because they could not reach the pots alone. However, in the spring, something was DIFFERENT. Jo grew TALLER! Jo was taller than El, so Jo could water the plants alone. El felt smaller every day. On the last day of school, Mr. Diaz said, "Class, you can take a flower home and care for it over the summer." All the students ran to the window. El's classmates reached for the pots over tiny El. They took all the pots with colorful flowers. El took the last pot. It had the smallest plant with no flowers. "I feel just like you, little plant," said El. Mr. Diaz looked at El and said, "That's an aster plant. In time, it'll grow and have beautiful flowers." "But it's just a little green plant," said El. She was not so sure. "You can have my zinnia plant," Jo said to El, "I'll be at my grandma's all summer." "I'll plant my aster and your zinnia side by side," El said. "They'll be good friends ― just like us!" said Jo. El smiled. El planted the flowers in her garden. It was growing season. All summer long, she cared for them. On the last day of summer, Jo came to El's house. El and Jo ran to the garden and suddenly stopped. Something was DIFFERENT! There were flowers on the aster ... and El grew TALLER, TOO!

items.q: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Jo는 여름 동안 할머니 댁에 있을 것이었다.
items.exp: El은 꽃이 없는 가장 작은 식물이 심긴 마지막 화분을 가져갔어요.

However, in the spring, something was DIFFERENT. Jo grew TALLER! Jo was taller than El, so Jo could water the plants alone. El felt smaller every day. They took all the pots with colorful flowers. El took the last pot. It had the smallest plant with no flowers. "I feel just like you, little plant," said El. Mr. Diaz looked at El and said, "That's an aster plant. In time, it'll grow and have beautiful flowers." "But it's just a little green plant," said El. She was not so sure. "You can have my zinnia plant," Jo said to El, "I'll be at my grandma's all summer." "I'll plant my aster and your zinnia side by side," El said. "They'll be good friends ― just like us!" said Jo. El smiled. El planted the flowers in her garden. It was growing season. All summer long, she cared for them. On the last day of summer, Jo came to El's house. El and Jo ran to the garden and suddenly stopped. Something was DIFFERENT! There were flowers on the aster ... and El grew TALLER, TOO!

items.q:
다음 질문에 대한 답으로 알맞은 것은?

What happened on the last day of summer?
choices: The aster had flowers, and El grew taller.
El gave her aster to Jo.
items.exp: 여름의 마지막 날 Jo가 El의 집에 왔고, 정원에 가 보니 aster에 꽃이 피었고 El도 키가 자라 있었어요.
items.passage: El planted the flowers in her garden. It was growing season. All summer long, she cared for them. On the last day of summer, Jo came to El's house. El and Jo ran to the garden and suddenly stopped. Something was DIFFERENT! There were flowers on the aster ... and El grew TALLER, TOO!

items.q:
글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

El got a plant with no (A), but after the summer, the aster had flowers and El grew (B), too.
items.exp: El의 식물은 꽃이 없었지만(no flowers), 여름이 지나자 꽃이 피었고 El도 키가 자랐어요(taller).

items.passage: Mr. Diaz looked at El and said, "That's an aster plant. In time, it'll grow and have beautiful flowers." "But it's just a little green plant," said El. She was not so sure.

items.passage: "You can have my zinnia plant," Jo said to El, "I'll be at my grandma's all summer." "I'll plant my aster and your zinnia side by side," El said. "They'll be good friends ― just like us!" said Jo. El smiled.

items.q: 어법상 틀린 문장은?
choices: He likes to visit big cities.

items.passage: I like studying with my friends, but Raon likes studying alone. However, we both like visiting big cities!

items.q: 형용사와 비교급의 형태가 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
items.exp: 짧은 단어는 -er을 붙여 longer, faster가 되고, popular처럼 긴 단어는 앞에 more를 붙여 more popular가 돼요.
